title: Kafka — Unified Observability
description: Everything about Kafka on one board, in the pack's order: SLIs and SLOs, MTTD/MTTR and certification, policy and alerting, remediation, signals, pipeline, logs and traces.

options.content:
### Kafka · Unified Observability
One board in the pack's own order: SLIs and SLOs, the validation that proves them (MTTD, MTTR, certification, synthetic checks), policy and alerting, remediation, the signals underneath, the pipeline, logs and traces.  ·  pack `kafka@1.0.0`  ·  **Unified** · [Cluster overview](/d/kafka-cluster-overview?${__url_time_range}) · [Consumer lag](/d/kafka-consumer-lag?${__url_time_range}) · [Throughput](/d/kafka-throughput?${__url_time_range}) · [Slo burn](/d/kafka-slo-burn?${__url_time_range})

panels.title: Broker availability
panels.description: Fraction of brokers reporting ready vs. cluster's declared broker count. SLO 99.9 % over 30d.

panels.title: Partition replica health
panels.description: Fraction of partitions where all in-sync replicas (ISRs) are present, vs. total partitions. SLO 99.95 % over 30d.

panels.title: Consumer group lag seconds
panels.description: Maximum consumer-group lag (in seconds equivalent), per critical consumer group. Computed by dividing message-count lag by the consumer's rolling consumption rate. SLO 99 % over 7d.

panels.title: Produce latency p99
panels.description: 99th-percentile latency of Produce requests, server-side. SLO 99 % over 30d.

panels.title: Fetch latency p99
panels.description: 99th-percentile latency of FetchConsumer requests, server-side. SLO 99 % over 30d.

panels.title: Controller election rate
panels.description: Rate of controller elections per hour. Elevated controller churn signals broker instability or network issues that haven't yet shown up in broker-availability metrics. SLO 99 % over 7d.

panels.title: Error-budget burn · last hour
panels.description: 1 h error-budget burn rate per SLO: 1× consumes the budget exactly over the SLO window; amber at the smallest factor that alerts for that SLO, red at the largest (spec.policy).

panels.title: Burn rate · 5 m window
panels.description: Fast window: reacts within minutes; pages when both it and the slow window exceed the factor. Hover for per-SLO values.

panels.title: Burn rate · 1 h window
panels.description: Slow window: keeps burning for up to an hour after an incident by design.

panels.title: Last certification
panels.description: Verdict of the last `npm run certify` published to the alert-sink: PASS, WARN, FAIL or ERROR.

panels.title: Certified
panels.description: When the last certification run finished.

panels.title: MTTD p50
panels.description: Median time from fault injection to the alert webhook, across every expected alert of the chaos suite. Baseline p50 2 min (pack spec.baselines).

panels.title: MTTD p95
panels.description: 95th percentile time to detect. Baseline p95 5 min.

panels.title: MTTR p50 · resolution
panels.description: Median time from the recovery action to the resolved webhook: the observability system's share of MTTR (it excludes the human/automation fix time). Baseline MTTR p50 30 min.

panels.title: MTTR p95 · resolution
panels.description: 95th percentile resolution after recovery. Baseline MTTR p95 60 min.

panels.title: MTTD per expected alert · against its budget
panels.description: Time from injection to the firing webhook for each expected alert in the last run; amber from 75 % of the experiment's expected_mttd, red at the budget.

panels.title: Resolution after recovery · per alert
panels.description: Time from the recovery action to the resolved webhook in the last run (Prometheus resolve + Alertmanager group_interval + webhook).

panels.title: Conformance passed
panels.description: C1-C10: does the stack implement the pack?

panels.title: Synthetic passed
panels.description: S1-S6: canary, orders flow, no symptom or fast-window burn alert firing.

panels.title: Chaos passed
panels.description: Experiments whose alerts fired within budget, resolved after recovery, and whose hypothesis SLI moved as declared.

panels.title: Webhooks in the ledger
panels.description: Alertmanager webhook events held by the alert-sink (MTTD is measured from their receipt time).

options.content:
| Check | Kind | Target | Interval | Assertions | On fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `produce-consume-canary` | k6 | `kafka.internal:9092` | 1m | produce_success=true; round_trip_latency_lt=500ms; payload_match=canary-${TIMESTAMP} | SEV2 |
| `consumer-group-health` | k6 | `kafka.internal:9092` | 1m | consumer_groups_assigned=true; current_offset_advancing=true | SEV2 |

<small>Declared in the pack's `validation.synthetic_checks`; the pack module supplies the panels that show the probes' own metrics.</small>

targets.expr: count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", pack="kafka", burn_rate="", kind=""}) or vector(0)

panels.title: Symptom alerts · pending / firing
panels.description: State of every symptom alert of the pack over the time range.

targets.expr: (2 * max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="kafka", alertstate="firing", burn_rate="", kind=""})) or max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="kafka", alertstate="pending", burn_rate="", kind=""}) or label_replace(vector(0), "alertname", "no alert", "", "")

panels.title: Firing pack alerts
panels.description: Everything currently firing with the pack label, most severe first.

panels.title: Burn-rate & forecast alerts · pending / firing
panels.description: Multi-window burn-rate alerts (fast windows page, slow windows linger after incidents) and forecasts.

targets.expr: (2 * max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="kafka", alertstate="firing", burn_rate!=""})) or max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="kafka", alertstate="pending", burn_rate!=""}) or label_replace(vector(0), "alertname", "no alert", "", "")
(2 * max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="kafka", alertstate="firing", kind="forecast"})) or max by (alertname) (ALERTS{pack="kafka", alertstate="pending", kind="forecast"})

options.content:
| Trigger | Runbook | Automation (declared) | Guardrails (declared) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kafka-broker-down` | `runbooks/broker-down.md` | `restart-broker-with-quorum-check` | ≤ 2/h · human above SEV1 · cooldown 30m |
| `kafka-partition-under-replicated` | `runbooks/under-replicated-partitions.md` | `reassign-partitions-with-throttle` | ≤ 1/h · human above SEV2 · cooldown 1h |
| `kafka-consumer-lag-burn` | `runbooks/consumer-lag.md` | `consumer-group-scale-out` | ≤ 3/h · human above SEV2 · cooldown 15m |
| `kafka-controller-churn` | `runbooks/controller-churn.md` | `manual-only` | ≤ 1/h · human above SEV2 |

<small>Automations and guardrails come from the pack's `remediation` section for the platform to implement; in this lab every action is done by hand, as the runbooks say.</small>
Derived view `golden_signals_kafka`: no metric or SLI to render.

panels.title: Per topic throughput
panels.description: Per-resource rollup of kafka_server_BrokerTopicMetrics_messagesinpersec by topic (pack derived view per_topic_throughput).

panels.title: Per consumergroup lag
panels.description: SLI consumer_group_lag_seconds by consumergroup (pack derived view per_consumergroup_lag).

panels.title: TSDB series
panels.description: Active series in the metrics store.

panels.title: Recording rules producing
panels.description: Distinct kafka:* recording-rule series currently produced (pack queries + generated error-budget rules).

panels.title: Scrape duration by job
panels.description: The pack's scrape jobs: kafka-broker, kafka-exporter.

panels.title: Collector · exported per second
panels.description: OpenTelemetry Collector export throughput (present when the pack pipeline runs through a collector).

panels.title: Collector · export failures per second
panels.description: The failure counters only exist once a batch has failed; a flat zero is the collector saying nothing has.

panels.title: Recent traces
panels.description: Traces whose resource is the kafka service.
